q: The Hamiltonian formulation of classical mechanics uses the Legendre transform to pass from Lagrangian L(q,q̇,t) to Hamiltonian H(q,p,t). The canonical equations are:
exp: Hamilton's equations: q̇ = ∂H/∂p (velocity from momentum), ṗ = −∂H/∂q (force = negative gradient of H). These are first-order equations on phase space (q,p) ∈ T*M. They preserve the symplectic form dq∧dp and (when H has no explicit t-dependence) the total energy H.
